title: Finite-basis hypercover existence on a site with fibre products
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with fibre products, and let $\mathcal B\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ be a set of objects. Assume every object $T$ has a finite covering $\{B_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ with all $B_i\in\mathcal B$. Assume also that adjoining one arrow $B\to T$ with $B\in\mathcal B$ to any finite covering with members in $\mathcal B$ again gives a covering. Then for each $T\in\mathcal C$ there exists an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] $K$ in the category of formal coproducts $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C/T)$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], with $K_n=\{B_{n,i}\to T\}_{i\in I_n}$, every $I_n$ finite and every $B_{n,i}\in\mathcal B$, whose matching arrows are coverings in every degree. A family morphism $(\alpha,f_i):\{A_i\}\to\{D_j\}$ is a covering here precisely when $\{f_i:A_i\to D_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ covers $D_j$ for each $j$. Matching objects are limits of the compatible proper-face diagram in $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C/T)$, with degree-zero matching object the one-member family $\{\operatorname{id}_T\}$. In particular all face and degeneracy maps satisfy the simplicial identities.

proof.text: Fix T. The category D=C/T has terminal object id_T, and a fibre product in D is the fibre product in C with its induced arrow to T: the universal property in C gives the unique arrow over T. Covering families in D are exactly families covering their target in C. Thus both finite B-cover hypotheses hold in D. Choose a finite B-cover K_0 of T; with only the identity operator it is a split 0-truncation (the nondegenerate indices are all of I_0). Its matching arrow to {id_T} is a covering by the componentwise convention in the item.

source.place: Tag 0DAV, lemma-hypercovering-object, first three proof paragraphs

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks], D has finite limits. Directly from [def-weil-pbc-formal-coproduct], the terminal family in SR(D) is {id_T}, and the pullback of (alpha,f):{A_i}-> {Z_k} and (beta,g):{B_j}-> {Z_k} is {A_i x_{Z_k} B_j}_{alpha(i)=k=beta(j)}: a map to it consists exactly of a pair of component maps with equal composite. This proves its universal property. For finite index sets this pullback has finite index set. Apply the same finite-limit lemma to the full subcategory of finite-index families, which has this terminal object and these pullbacks. Thus every finite boundary diagram on finite-index terms has a finite-index limit M, also a limit in SR(D), since the terminal and pullback universal properties just checked hold against arbitrary source families. No degree n+1 term is assumed here.

proof.text: Inductively suppose a split n-truncation K has finite B-terms and covering matching arrows in degrees 0 through n. Write the next matching limit from step 2 as M={W_h}_{h in H}, with H finite. For every h choose a finite B-cover {V_{h,j}->W_h}_{j in J_h}. Let V be their disjoint-union family and v:V->M its componentwise map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-hypercover-finite-extension] in D: its explicitly defined split hypothesis is the induction invariant, and its boundary diagram is exactly this M. The resulting L extends K, with new nondegenerate terms V and degenerate copies of the U_{r,i} for r<=n. All components remain in B. The new index set is finite because H and every J_h and N_r are finite, and there are finitely many order-preserving surjections between the displayed finite ordered sets. The cited attachment theorem supplies all operators and their composition identities; no identity is inferred merely from choosing covers.

source.place: Tag 0DAV, lemma-hypercovering-object, construction of the extension

proof.text: For each h, the fibre of the new matching family over W_h contains its chosen finite B-cover, together with finitely many arrows from the prescribed degenerate copies. Starting with that cover, adjoin these arrows one at a time. At every stage the family is finite, all domains lie in B, and the adjoining hypothesis applies, so the final family is a cover of W_h. This includes H empty (there is then no covering condition to check) and an empty chosen cover (the same adjoining hypothesis still applies). Thus L has a covering matching arrow in degree n+1; the earlier arrows are unchanged because L restricts to K.

source.place: Tag 0DAV, lemma-hypercovering-object, paragraph proving K_{n+1}->K′_{n+1} is a covering

proof.text: Starting from step 1, recursively choose extensions by steps 2-4. Define K_q to be its permanent value at stage q, and define each operator [a]->[b] using any stage at least max(a,b); extensions agree exactly in lower degrees, so this is independent of the stage. For composable operators choose a stage containing all three degrees: the functor identity there proves their composition identity in K. The same argument proves identity operators. Every fixed degree has finite B-components and a covering matching arrow from its construction stage. The arrows to T give the augmentation to {id_T}; they commute with every operator because every construction was in C/T. Degree zero has matching object {id_T}, as required.

lean.statement: theorem exists_site_finite_basis_hypercover {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [HasPullbacks C] (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition] [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] (B : Set C) (hcover : ∀ T : C, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ T), Finite I ∧ (∀ i : I, U i ∈ B) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J T) (hadjoin : ∀ (T : C) (I : Type u) [Finite I] (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ T), (∀ i : I, U i ∈ B) → Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J T → ∀ (V : C), V ∈ B → ∀ (g : V ⟶ T), Presieve.ofArrows U f ⊔ Presieve.singleton g ∈ J T) (T : C) : ∃ (K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{u} (Over T))) (M : ∀ n : ℕ, Cone (K.properFaceDiagram n)) (μ : ∀ n : ℕ, K _⦋n⦌ ⟶ (M n).pt), (∀ n : ℕ, Finite (K _⦋n⦌).I) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : (K _⦋n⦌).I), ((K _⦋n⦌).obj i).left ∈ B) ∧ (M 0).pt = (FormalCoproduct.incl (Over T)).obj (Over.mk (𝟙 T)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (IsLimit (M n))) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : SimplicialObject.ProperFaceCategory n), μ n ≫ (M n).π.app (op a) = K.map a.obj.hom.op) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : (M n).pt.I), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i : {i : (K _⦋n⦌).I // (μ n).f i = j} ↦ ((K _⦋n⦌).obj i.val).left) (fun i : {i : (K _⦋n⦌).I // (μ n).f i = j} ↦ ((μ n).φ i.val).left ≫ eqToHom (congrArg (fun k ↦ ((M n).pt.obj k).left) i.property)) ∈ J ((M n).pt.obj j).left)
lean.note: The existing properFaceDiagram is used directly (landed statement dependency added under brief-stage2 §5). Matching cones and their canonical arrows are quantified with IsLimit and the projection equations; covering is the original precoverage condition on each index fibre. Simplicial objects in formal families of Over T carry the augmentation canonically.
